$\begin{aligned} & -\frac{\mathrm{d}\left[\mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{O}_5\right]}{\mathrm{dt}}=\mathrm{K}_1\left[\mathrm{~N}_2 \mathrm{O}_5\right] \\ & +\frac{\mathrm{d}\left[\mathrm{NO}_2\right]}{\mathrm{dt}}=\mathrm{K}_2\left[\mathrm{~N}_2 \mathrm{O}_5\right] \\ & +\frac{\mathrm{d}\left[\mathrm{O}_2\right]}{\mathrm{dt}}=\mathrm{K}_3\left[\mathrm{~N}_2 \mathrm{O}_5\right]\end{aligned}$
The correct relation between $\mathrm{K}_1, \mathrm{~K}_2$ and $\mathrm{K}_3$ is
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} &  \mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{O}_5 \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{NO}_2+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{O}_2 \\ & \text { Rate of reaction }=-\frac{\mathrm{d}\left[\mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{O}_5\right]}{\mathrm{dt}}=\frac{1}{2} \frac{\mathrm{~d}\left[\mathrm{NO}_2\right]}{\mathrm{dt}}=2 \frac{\mathrm{~d}\left[\mathrm{O}_2\right]}{\mathrm{dt}} \\ & \therefore \quad \mathrm{K}_1\left[\mathrm{~N}_2 \mathrm{O}_5\right]=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{~K}_2\left[\mathrm{~N}_2 \mathrm{O}_5\right]=2 \mathrm{~K}_3\left[\mathrm{~N}_2 \mathrm{O}_5\right] \\ & \therefore 2 \mathrm{~K}_1=\mathrm{K}_2=4 \mathrm{~K}_3\end{aligned}$

questions.q: At 300 K , the vapour pressure of toluene and benzene are 3.63 kPa and 9.7 kPa respectively. What is the composition of vapour in equilibrium with the solution containing 0.4 mole fraction of toluene? (Assume the solution is ideal)

$\begin{aligned}
&  \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{T}}^0=3.63 \mathrm{kPa} \quad \mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{A}}=0.4 \quad\left[\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{A}}+\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{B}}=1\right] \\
& \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{B}}=9.7 \mathrm{kPa} \quad \mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{A}}=0.6 \\
& \therefore \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{T}}=\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{A}}^0+\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{B}}^0 \\
& =\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{T}}^0 \mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{A}}+\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{B}}^0 \mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{B}} \Rightarrow 3.63 \times 0.4+9.7 \times 0.6
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
& =1.452+5.82 \\
& \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{T}}=7.272
\end{aligned}\therefore$ Composition of toluene $\left(\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{T}}\right)=\frac{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{A}}}{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{T}}}\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{T}} & =\frac{1.452}{7.272} \\
\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{T}} & =0.1996 \\
\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{T}} & \approx 0.20
\end{aligned}$

Also, $\tan \mathrm{h}^{-1}(x)=\frac{1}{2} \log \left(\frac{1-x}{1+x}\right)\tan \mathrm{h}^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)=\frac{1}{2} \log \left(\frac{1-\frac{3}{5}}{1+\frac{3}{5}}\right)=\frac{1}{2} \log \frac{2}{8}=\frac{1}{2} \log \frac{1}{4}=\log \frac{1}{2}$ Hence, $\operatorname{sech}^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)+\tan h^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)=\log 3+\log \frac{1}{2}=\log \frac{3}{2} .$

questions.q: The equation $16 x^4+16 x^3-4 x-1=0$ has a multiple root. If $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta$ are the roots of this equation, then $\frac{1}{\alpha^4}+\frac{1}{\beta^4}+\frac{1}{\gamma^4}+\frac{1}{\delta^4}=$
questions.solution:
Given: $16 x^4+16 x^3-4 x-1=0=f(x)$ has a multiple root.
Let $\alpha=\beta$ be the multiple root. Since $\alpha$ is root of $f(x) \quad \therefore f(\alpha)=0\Rightarrow 16 \alpha^4+16 \alpha^3-4 \alpha-1=0$ ...(i) As $\alpha$ is multiple root $\Rightarrow f^{\prime}(\alpha)=0$ Now, $f^{\prime}(x)=64 x^3+48 x^2-4 \Rightarrow f^{\prime}(\alpha)=0\Rightarrow 64 \alpha^3+48 \alpha^2-4=0 \Rightarrow 16 \alpha^3+12 \alpha^2-1=0$ ...(ii) Subtracting (ii) from (i), $16 \alpha^4-12 \alpha^2+1-4 \alpha-1=0\Rightarrow 16 \alpha^4-12 \alpha^2-4 \alpha=0 \Rightarrow 4 \alpha\left(4 \alpha^3-3 \alpha-1\right)=0\alpha \neq 0$ as it doesn't satisfy given equation $\Rightarrow \cdot 4 \alpha^3-3 \alpha-1=0 \Rightarrow(\alpha-1)(2 \alpha+1)^2=0\alpha \neq 1$ as it doesn't satisfy given equation $\Rightarrow 2 \alpha+1=0 \Rightarrow \alpha=\frac{-1}{2}$ So, $\alpha=\frac{-1}{2}$ is a root of the given equation By using synthetic division $\Rightarrow g(x)=16 x^3+8 x^2-4 x-2$ Since, $\alpha=\frac{-1}{2}$ is multiple root By using synthetic division again $\Rightarrow h(x)=16 x^2-4=0\Rightarrow x^2=\frac{4}{16}=\frac{1}{4} \Rightarrow x= \pm \frac{1}{2}$
Hence, $\alpha=\frac{-1}{2}, \beta=\frac{-1}{2}, \gamma=\frac{-1}{2}, \delta=\frac{1}{2}$ So, $\frac{1}{\alpha^4}+\frac{1}{\beta^4}+\frac{1}{\gamma^4}+\frac{1}{\delta^4}=2^4+2^4+2^4+2^4=16+16+16+16=64 .$
